cleanIntro: The SSG 08 is a magazine-fed bolt rifle with a folding stock and Steyr's rotary "2 + 1" safety. Steyr's own SSG 08 book publishes exactly one strip, which is the bolt out of the receiver. It also says complete disassembly of the rifle by the user is usually not required. ⛔ The barrel is the part this rifle is won or lost on. Steyr says never use a steel brush, always clean chamber to muzzle, and take the patch off AT the muzzle. An oversized patch or brush can dislodge the rotary bushing between barrel and receiver, and then the bolt will not go in.

steps.title: Rotary safety to SAFE — only the white dot showing
steps.action: Turn the rotary safety on the butt neck back to "Safe", so only the white dot is visible. In this position an unintended shot is prevented and the bolt can still be worked to unload.
steps.prose: Steyr's "Lock" position (grey lock showing) locks the bolt shut. Unloading is done on Safe, not on Lock.
steps.quote: 1. Move rotary safety in position “Safe“ (Fig. 7 only white dot is visible).
steps.cite: INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE / BETRIEBSANLEITUNG — STEYR SSG 08 — Edition EU 06, 1-BA-6003 (printed on the cover) — 9. Loading / unloading — Unloading, step 1, p.24

steps.title: Magazine out — squeeze BOTH snap latches together
steps.action: Press the two snap latches on the right and left of the magazine fully together with thumb and index finger of one hand, and draw the magazine out while you keep pressing. Steyr also allows locking it in the second position, where it stands about 5 mm proud and will not feed. For cleaning, take it out.
steps.prose: The magazine has two locked positions, and the second one looks almost seated. Out is the only state you can see is empty.
steps.quote: Press the two snap latches at the right and the left of the magazine fully together using thumb and index finger of one hand and remove the magazine while pressing.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE / BETRIEBSANLEITUNG — STEYR SSG 08 — Edition EU 06, 1-BA-6003 (printed on the cover) — 7. Removing the magazine, p.19

steps.title: Bolt open and back — then LOOK in the chamber
steps.action: Open the bolt handle and draw the bolt back so any round in the chamber is extracted and ejected. Then look into the chamber and make certain it is empty.
steps.prose: Ejected is not the same as empty. The check is your eyes on the chamber.
steps.quote: 3. By opening the bolt handle and retracting the bolt, the cartridge located in the loading chamber of the barrel will be extracted and ejected. Make certain that no cartridge is in the chamber.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE / BETRIEBSANLEITUNG — STEYR SSG 08 — Edition EU 06, 1-BA-6003 (printed on the cover) — 9. Loading / unloading — Unloading, step 3, p.24
steps.warn: Before cleaning unload the weapon and conduct safety check.

steps.title: Fold the stock — push the button DOWN, swing the stock LEFT
steps.action: Push the stock button fully down and swing the stock to the left. The folded stock is out of the way of the bolt.
steps.prose: Steyr recommends taking the bolt out for proper barrel cleaning, and folding the stock is the first move of that procedure.
steps.aside: Removal of the bolt is recommended to facilitate proper cleaning of the barrel.
steps.quote: 1. Push down the button completely and swing the stock to the left.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE / BETRIEBSANLEITUNG — STEYR SSG 08 — Edition EU 06, 1-BA-6003 (printed on the cover) — 10. Removing the bolt, step 1, p.25

steps.title: Unlock the bolt, safety to LOCK, draw the bolt out by its handle
steps.action: With your right hand, turn the bolt handle 70° to unlock. Move the rotary safety to "Lock", where the grey lock snaps out. Then hold the bolt by its handle and draw it out of the receiver.
steps.prose: The order is Steyr's own: unlock, then Lock, then out. It goes back in with the safety on Lock too.
steps.aside: 3. Move rotary safety to position “Lock“ (Fig. 8 gray lock snaps out).
steps.quote: 4. Hold bolt by the bolt handle and extract it from the receiver.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE / BETRIEBSANLEITUNG — STEYR SSG 08 — Edition EU 06, 1-BA-6003 (printed on the cover) — 10. Removing the bolt, step 4, p.25

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The magazine and bolt are out and the stock is folded. That is Steyr's whole strip for cleaning. The two screws under the rifle hold the receiver to the stock. Steyr says complete disassembly is usually not required, and that if those screws are loosened they go back to 7 Nm with a torque wrench. ⛔ The hex screw at the front bottom of the receiver is never loosened. The bolt's own disassembly is under DEEP CLEAN.
steps.prose: Steyr writes that the action is designed to need no maintenance for long periods. Cleaning this rifle is about the barrel.
steps.quote: Complete disassembly of the rifle by the user usually is not required.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE / BETRIEBSANLEITUNG — STEYR SSG 08 — Edition EU 06, 1-BA-6003 (printed on the cover) — 13. Disassembling the rifle, p.28
steps.warn: When removing the action from the rifle, the hex screw at the front bottom side of the receiver must never be loosened.

deepSteps.title: Know first: the bolt is factory-lubricated and rarely needs opening
deepSteps.action: Steyr's position is that under normal circumstances the bolt does not need to be taken apart, because it is permanently lubricated at the factory. Occasional inspection by a Steyr dealer's gunsmith is the usual maintenance. Only when no gunsmith is available should you open it yourself.
deepSteps.prose: Steyr also offers that an expert gunsmith can show you the bolt disassembly. That is the maker's preferred route.
deepSteps.quote: Under normal circumstances, the bolt doesn’t need to be disassembled. It has been permanently lubricated by the factory.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE / BETRIEBSANLEITUNG — STEYR SSG 08 — Edition EU 06, 1-BA-6003 (printed on the cover) — 14. Disassembling the bolt, p.29

deepSteps.title: Bolt sleeve off — catch lever IN, rotate CLOCKWISE to the click
deepSteps.action: Grip the bolt in your left hand. Push in the catch lever with your right thumb and at the same time rotate the bolt sleeve clockwise until it unlocks with an audible click.
deepSteps.prose: The direction is the whole step. Clockwise only.
deepSteps.quote: 1. Grip the bolt with your left hand. Push in catch lever with your right thumb and simultaneously rotate the bolt sleeve clockwise (arrow shows direction of rotation) until it unlocks with an audible click.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE / BETRIEBSANLEITUNG — STEYR SSG 08 — Edition EU 06, 1-BA-6003 (printed on the cover) — 14. Disassembling the bolt, step 1, p.29
deepSteps.warn: When disassembling, never rotate the bolt sleeve in counterclockwise direction. Otherwise, the bolt could not be reinserted into the receiver.

deepSteps.title: Firing pin assembly out — and STOP there
deepSteps.action: Take off the bolt sleeve and draw out the firing pin assembly. All the bolt parts can then be cleaned and oiled. ⛔ Steyr's book stops here. Anything further is for trained, skilled personnel.
deepSteps.prose: Reassembly is the reverse. The firing pin lug sits directly opposite the bolt handle, and the bolt cap is turned counterclockwise until it locks, but no further than the alignment line.
deepSteps.aside: Any further disassembly should be done only by adequately trained and skilled personnel (gunsmith).
deepSteps.quote: 2. Take off bolt sleeve and extract firing pin assembly.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE / BETRIEBSANLEITUNG — STEYR SSG 08 — Edition EU 06, 1-BA-6003 (printed on the cover) — 14. Disassembling the bolt, step 2, p.29

deepSteps.title: Past 70 rounds: alternate a COPPER solvent and a CARBON remover
deepSteps.action: After more than 70 rounds, take out the heavy fouling. Copper shows from the muzzle as a copper-coloured residue, and carbon as black between the lands. Alternate a copper solvent and a carbon remover, used as their makers direct, with the bronze brush and patches. Keep going until a fresh wet patch comes through clean. Copper residue shows blue and carbon shows grey.
deepSteps.prose: Steyr gives the reason. Heavy fouling raises barrel pressure, which brings hard extraction and lost accuracy, and can make the rifle unsafe.
deepSteps.aside: 4. Repeat this alternating operation with the copper solvent and the carbon remover until a new solvent-moistened patch can be passed through the bore remaining clean (copper residue is blue colored, carbon residue is gray colored).
deepSteps.quote: Remove heavy fouling deposits after firing a large number of rounds (more than 70 rounds).
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE / BETRIEBSANLEITUNG — STEYR SSG 08 — Edition EU 06, 1-BA-6003 (printed on the cover) — Cleaning of the bore (after firing more than 70 rounds), p.40

cleaning.name: BORE — UP TO 70 ROUNDS
tasks: Magazine out, rifle unloaded and checked, laid flat on a rigid board
Clean rod, patch wet with bore solvent pushed right through, chamber to muzzle
⛔ Patch taken off at the muzzle, never pulled back through
Correct-size bronze brush through the wet bore after the dwell time: one back-and-forth cycle for every three rounds fired
Patches through chamber and bore until a wet patch stays clean; last of the solvent out with a dry patch

cleaning.name: CHAMBER, RECEIVER, COMPENSATOR
tasks: Chamber cleaned with a fitting brush or a rod section
Bore cleaned AFTER the chamber, to clear the solvent
Surplus solvent wiped from the receiver and the compensator

cleaning.name: OIL AND STORAGE
tasks: Bore and chamber oiled slightly for long storage or a corrosive atmosphere
⛔ Oil out of bore and chamber with a dry patch before shooting, or the point of impact shifts
Outer metal surfaces slightly oiled; scope mount kept clean and slightly oiled

cleaning.name: LEAVE ALONE
tasks: ⛔ No steel brushes in the barrel
⛔ No oversized patches or brushes, which can dislodge the rotary bushing so the bolt will not lock
⛔ No solvents or insect repellents on the synthetic parts
⛔ The hex screw at the front bottom of the receiver is never loosened
⛔ Trigger adjustment is for a Steyr armorer only
⛔ No bolt disassembly beyond the firing pin assembly

reassembly: Firing pin assembly into the bolt with the firing pin lug directly opposite the bolt handle (if removed).
Bolt cap slid onto the firing pin lug while pressing the ratchet lever, then turned counterclockwise until it locks, and not past the alignment line.
Rifle confirmed unloaded, magazine out or in its second position.
Rotary safety on "Lock"; bolt inserted by its handle, rotated so the handle slides into the receiver slot.
Safety to "Fire", then the bolt handle locked down while pulling the trigger so the firing pin is not cocked. The indicator pin at the rear of the bolt sleeve disappears.
fncheck: With the magazine out and the chamber confirmed empty: work the bolt through its full travel and lock it down. Move the rotary safety back to "Lock" (grey lock showing) and confirm the bolt handle will not open. Move it to "Safe" (white dot only) and confirm the bolt can be worked. Insert the empty magazine in its normal position and check it locks with an audible click and sits flush with the stock. ⛔ Before shooting, Steyr says to remove the oil from the bore and chamber with a dry, clean patch. Oil left there shifts the point of impact.
